login.hintBound: After signing in with the admin token you act as the linked GitHub account {login}. Use it only when GitHub sign-in is unavailable.
login.hintUnbound: The first time, sign in with the admin token, then link your GitHub account under Settings → Sign-in & identity.
login.hintTokenOff: Admin token sign-in is turned off. If GitHub sign-in becomes unavailable, an administrator can run kiln admin token-login on on the server to restore it.
login.hintConfigureOAuth: Once GitHub sign-in (KILN_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID) is configured, you and other members can sign in with GitHub accounts.
login.signedIn: You're signed in as {login} ({role}). You can continue, or sign in as someone else below.
login.noticeExpired: Your session has expired. Sign in again to return to the page you were on.
login.noticeRevoked: Your session is no longer valid: an administrator changed the sign-in methods or account permissions (for example, turned off admin token sign-in). Sign in again.
login.errTokenDisabled: Admin token sign-in is turned off. Sign in with GitHub.
login.errTokenInvalid: The admin token is incorrect; you weren't signed in. Check that you copied all of it (no spaces or line breaks).
error.serverHeading: Something went wrong on the server
error.serverReasonGet: An internal error occurred while handling this request. The details are in the server log. You can try again later; if the problem persists, give the error ID below to an administrator.
error.serverReasonPost: An internal error occurred while handling this action, so it may not have completed. The details are in the server log. Go back to the previous page and check the result before deciding whether to retry; if the problem persists, give the error ID below to an administrator.
error.notFoundReason: The address may be mistyped, or what you're looking for no longer exists.
error.forbiddenReason: Only administrators can use this page or action. You're signed in as {login}, a member, and nothing was done. Contact an administrator if needed, or sign in again as an administrator.
error.csrfHeading: The page has expired; nothing was done
error.csrfReason: The form's security check (CSRF) failed, usually because the page was open too long, you signed in again in the meantime, or the form came from another site. Go back to the previous page, refresh it, and try again.
error.oauthDisabledReason: This Server has no GitHub sign-in configured (KILN_GITHUB_CLIENT_ID). Administrators can sign in with the admin token on the sign-in page.
error.oauthInvalidReason: The parameters returned by GitHub sign-in are invalid or were modified (for example, an old or incomplete link was opened), so you weren't signed in. Go back to the sign-in page and sign in again.
error.oauthOtherBrowserReason: This GitHub authorization wasn't started in this browser (for example, you opened a link someone sent you, or opened the callback address in another browser), so you weren't signed in. Sign in with GitHub again from the sign-in page.

error.oauthExpiredReason.one: More than {count, number} minute passed between opening the GitHub authorization page and returning to Kiln, so it didn't complete. Please try again.
error.oauthExpiredReason.other: More than {count, number} minutes passed between opening the GitHub authorization page and returning to Kiln, so it didn't complete. Please try again.

error.oauthDeniedReason: GitHub didn't complete the authorization (for example, Cancel was clicked on the authorization page), so nothing was signed in or linked. You can try again.
error.oauthNoAccessHeading: This GitHub account doesn't have access
error.oauthNoAccessReason: The GitHub account {login} isn't the account linked by the administrator and isn't on Kiln's member or administrator lists (KILN_USERS / KILN_ADMINS), so you weren't signed in. Ask an administrator to add it; to use a different account, sign out of GitHub first and then sign in again.
error.oauthFailedReason: Kiln couldn't get your account information from GitHub (a network problem, GitHub being temporarily unavailable, or an authorization code that was already used), so sign-in didn't complete. You can retry; if the problem persists, give the error ID to an administrator.
error.bindInvalidReason: This GitHub authorization wasn't started by the administrator who is currently signed in (for example, the link was opened in another browser, or you signed in again in the meantime), so nothing was linked. Link the account again under Settings → Sign-in & identity.
account.bound: Linked GitHub account {login}. You're now signed in as {login}.
account.unbound: Unlinked. Admin token sign-in has been restored.
copy.label: Copy

api.unauthorized: Your session has expired. Sign in again.

overview.setupRunnerText: Runners run on your own machines and only make outbound connections to the server. You need at least one to start building.
overview.setupBindText: Once linked, signing in with GitHub makes you an administrator, and your actions are recorded under that account.
overview.setupTokenText: After confirming that GitHub sign-in works, turn this off so the Dashboard only accepts GitHub sign-in.

rerun.hintRetry.other: {count, number} jobs that didn't succeed (failed, cancelled, skipped) are replanned; jobs with unchanged inputs still hit the cache;

rerun.hintNoCache.other: All {count, number} jobs are forced to run again without reading the cache. Use this when you suspect a cached result is wrong; it takes the longest.

rerun.title: Re-run this run
rerun.intro: Creates a new run on the same commit, based on the results of the latest one ({rerun}, {state}). Workflow files come from this commit; variables, secrets, and environments use the current configuration. Existing runs are kept, and you can switch between them in the top right.
rerun.purged: The latest run's outputs were cleaned up under the retention policy, so successful jobs can't reuse their results and are replanned too (they may still hit the cache if inputs are unchanged). Only successful publish jobs reuse their results and won't publish again.
rerun.keepHint: Keeps the job's state on the runner after a failure so you can log in and investigate.
run.pickerInvalid: The run you're viewing is invalid; switch to another run
run.mqQueuedText: PR #{pr} is in the merge queue and merges automatically once it passes verification and isn't behind the target branch.
run.mqRemovedText: Add the label again or add it on the merge queue page to retry.

run.invalidOne.one: This run has run {count, number} time: {first}. <link>View the latest</link>
run.invalidOne.other: This run has run {count, number} times: {first}. <link>View the latest</link>

run.invalidRange.other: This run has run {count, number} times: {first} to {last}. <link>View the latest</link>

run.historyText: The latest is {rerun}, {state}. <link>View the latest</link>. Cancel and re-run in the top right always act on the latest run.
run.purgedText: This run finished longer ago than the retention period, so its logs and outputs were cleaned up at {time} under the retention policy. Only the results (status, duration, reason) are kept.
run.stages: ; {count, number} stages by dependency, run left to right
run.emptyJobsConfig: This run has no jobs (configuration error).
run.enqueueTitle: Add PR #{pr} to the merge queue?
run.enqueueText: Kiln adds the label kiln:merge to the PR and verifies its head in queue order. It merges automatically once CI and AI review both pass and the PR isn't behind the target branch; if it's behind, Kiln updates the PR branch first and merges after the new head passes verification.
run.cancelText: Cancels {rerun} of this run: running jobs are stopped and jobs that haven't started won't run. Finished jobs aren't affected, and releases or images that were already published aren't withdrawn.

runNew.targetErrHint: You can enter the workflow file name directly.

runNew.workflowFileRefHint: After fixing the ref, click "Load workflows" to choose from a list.

runNew.fromFilter: Preselected from the run list filter; please confirm.
runNew.refHint: Leave empty for the default branch {branch}. You can enter a branch name, a tag name (such as v1.2.0), or a full ref (such as refs/tags/v1.2.0). After changing the ref, click "Load workflows" to refresh the list below.
runNew.inputsHint: One key=value per line; values may contain =, and empty lines are ignored. Inputs you leave out use the workflow's defaults. Inputs are saved with the run and shown on the Dashboard, so don't enter secrets.
runNew.publishNote: In manually triggered runs, publish jobs fail during planning: publishing can only be triggered by pushing a tag.
runNew.lead: Run a workflow that declares on.workflow_dispatch manually: choose a repository first, then a ref and a workflow.
logView.title: Log
logView.nextStep: This attempt has ended; waiting for the job's next step…
logView.retry: {why}. Retrying automatically in {seconds, number}s (attempt {n}); the log shown so far is kept.
logView.expired: Your session has expired; the log has stopped updating.
logView.notLog: The response wasn't log content (your session may have expired); updates have stopped.
logView.scope: Searches only the log loaded on the page, case-insensitively (Enter for next, Shift+Enter for previous). The page keeps at most the last ~2 million characters; download the full log for everything.
logView.switched: Attempt #{from} has ended; below is the log of the new attempt #{to}. <link>View the log of attempt #{from}</link>
logView.truncated: The log is too long; the page keeps only the last ~2 million characters and earlier output was dropped. <link>Download the full log</link>
job.logBlocked: Choose a valid attempt to show the log.
job.progressUnavailable: Progress isn't available: the runner executing this job doesn't report stages (it may be an older kiln-runner). See the log below.
job.progressTimes: {phase} in this stage · last progress {moved} ago
job.progressAwaiting: Everything has been sent; waiting for the server to verify it (the upload counts as done only after that).
job.progressStalled: No progress for {d} (still waiting; this doesn't mean it failed).
job.progressSilent: The runner hasn't reported for {d}; the above may be out of date.

job.queueAhead.one: <num>{count, number}</num> job is waiting to be picked up ahead of it; the first belongs to <link>Run #{run}</link>.
job.queueAhead.other: <num>{count, number}</num> jobs are waiting to be picked up ahead of it; the first belongs to <link>Run #{run}</link>.

job.queueNone: No jobs are ahead of it; waiting for a runner to pick it up.
job.queueRule: Counted in scheduling order: higher priority first, then runs submitted earlier at the same priority (re-runs by re-run time). Only waiting jobs with the same platform {platform} and executor {executor} are counted, whether or not they can run on the same runner.
job.attemptErrPick: <link>View the current attempt</link>, or choose one under "Attempts" below.
job.reusedText: Reused the result of an earlier run: <link>job #{job}</link> (this job didn't run again; its log and outputs come from that job)
job.cachedText: The result comes from <link>job #{job}</link> (cache hit; didn't run again)
job.viewingText: Attempt {n} (#{id}, {outcome}) isn't the current attempt. The job is currently: {state}. <link>View the current attempt</link>
job.openLatest: Open this job in the latest run
job.noLatest: The latest run doesn't have this job.
job.cancelText: This cancels the whole Run #{id} (not just this job): running jobs are stopped and jobs that haven't started won't run. Finished jobs aren't affected, and releases or images that were already published aren't withdrawn.
job.effectForce: This job succeeded last time, so it's forced to run again (without cache).
job.effectReplan: This job is replanned; it may still hit the cache if its inputs are unchanged.

job.effectDownstream.one: {count, number} downstream job is replanned too (cache allowed): {names}.
job.effectDownstream.other: {count, number} downstream jobs are replanned too (cache allowed): {names}.

job.effectKept.one: {count, number} other job reuses this run's result and doesn't run again.
job.effectKept.other: {count, number} other jobs reuse this run's results and don't run again.

job.effectPurged.one: This run's outputs were cleaned up under the retention policy, so {count, number} more successful job can't reuse its result and is replanned too (cache allowed).
job.effectPurged.other: This run's outputs were cleaned up under the retention policy, so {count, number} more successful jobs can't reuse their results and are replanned too (cache allowed).

job.effectNew: A new re-run is created (the next one after {rerun}).
job.effectPublish: The replanned jobs include a publish job, so publishing runs again (idempotent per tag: existing assets with identical content are skipped).
job.rerunTitle: Re-run this job and its downstream jobs

job.moreFiles.other: {count, number} more files aren't listed (only the first {shown, number} by path are listed).

job.manifestMissing: The output manifest is no longer in storage, so outputs can't be listed or downloaded. Re-run this job (without cache) to regenerate them.
job.declaredFailed: Declared outputs: {names}. The job didn't succeed, so there are no outputs.
job.declaredPending: Declared outputs: {names}. You can download them here once the job succeeds.
job.noOutputs: This job doesn't declare outputs, so there are none.
job.releaseDraft: (notes.from: draft — kept as a draft; publish it manually on GitHub)
job.uploadPrevious: Already published earlier with identical content.
job.npmPrevious: Already published with identical content; not published again this time.
job.attemptsEmpty: Not started yet. Each attempt will be listed here once it starts, and the log appears automatically without reloading the page.
job.attemptsNote: Infrastructure errors (a runner disconnecting, environment setup failing, and so on) are retried automatically as new attempts; re-runs create new jobs and aren't counted here.
aiRunner.notFound: There is no AI runner named {name}.
runner.opUnknown: Unknown runner operation; nothing was done.
runnerOp.notFound: There is no runner named {name}; nothing was done.
runnerOp.notRevoked: {name} is not revoked; nothing was done. Revoke it before deleting it.
runnerOp.alreadyRevoked: {name} has already been revoked; nothing was done. To keep using this machine, register it again.
runnerOp.failedRef: The operation on {name} failed: something went wrong on the server (error ID {ref}) and the operation may not have completed. Check the result before deciding whether to retry; if the problem persists, give the error ID to an administrator.
runnerOp.drained: Paused {name}: it takes no new jobs once its current poll ends (at most about {poll, duration}). It has no running jobs; click “Resume” when needed.

runnerOp.drainedBusy.one: Paused {name}: it takes no new jobs once its current poll ends (at most about {poll, duration}). Its {count, number} running job continues to completion; click “Resume” when needed.
runnerOp.drainedBusy.other: Paused {name}: it takes no new jobs once its current poll ends (at most about {poll, duration}). Its {count, number} running jobs continue to completion; click “Resume” when needed.

runnerOp.undrained: {name} accepts jobs again and picks up new jobs when it has capacity.
runnerOp.undrainedOffline: {name} accepts jobs again, but it is offline; it picks up jobs after it reconnects.
runnerOp.deleted: Deleted {name}: it no longer appears in the list and the name can be registered again; attempts it ran still show this name.
runnerOp.revoked: Revoked {name}; all its further requests are rejected. To restore this machine, register it again.

runnerOp.revokedBusy.one: Revoked {name}; all its further requests are rejected. Its {count, number} running job is interrupted and, after about {lease, duration}, treated as a lost runner, an infrastructure error (usually requeued). To restore this machine, register it again.
runnerOp.revokedBusy.other: Revoked {name}; all its further requests are rejected. Its {count, number} running jobs are interrupted and, after about {lease, duration}, treated as a lost runner, an infrastructure error (most are requeued). To restore this machine, register it again.

runnerOp.revokedBusyAI.one: Revoked {name}; all its further requests are rejected. Its {count, number} running AI task is interrupted and ends as a lost runner after about {lease, duration}. To restore this machine, register it again.
runnerOp.revokedBusyAI.other: Revoked {name}; all its further requests are rejected. Its {count, number} running AI tasks are interrupted and end as a lost runner after about {lease, duration}. To restore this machine, register it again.

runnerNew.errKind: The runner type must be CI runner, AI review runner, or AI development runner
runnerNew.errPool: A pool may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens, must start with a letter or digit, and can be at most 64 characters long
runnerNew.errName: A name may contain only letters, digits, dots, underscores, and hyphens, must start with a letter or digit, and can be at most 64 characters long
runnerUpgrade.opUnknown: Unknown upgrade operation; nothing was done.
runnerUpgrade.requested: Requested upgrading {name} to {version}: the runner downloads and verifies it, switches after its running jobs finish, and the upgrade completes once the new version starts and is confirmed.
runnerUpgrade.requestedOffline: Requested upgrading {name} to {version}: the runner downloads and verifies it, switches after its running jobs finish, and the upgrade completes once the new version starts and is confirmed. It is offline now; the upgrade runs after it reconnects.
runnerUpgrade.alreadyRequested: {name} is already upgrading to {version}; no duplicate request was made.
runnerUpgrade.cancelled: Cancelled upgrading {name} to {version}; the downloaded package is kept and reused for a later upgrade.
runnerUpgrade.checkRequested: Asked {name} to check for the latest version: it checks the next time it contacts the server (at most about {poll, duration} while online).
runnerUpgrade.startFailedRef: Not upgraded: something went wrong on the server (error ID {ref}) and the operation may not have completed. Check the result before deciding whether to retry; if the problem persists, give the error ID to an administrator.
runnerUpgrade.cancelFailedRef: Not cancelled: something went wrong on the server (error ID {ref}) and the operation may not have completed. Check the result before deciding whether to retry; if the problem persists, give the error ID to an administrator.
runnerUpgrade.checkFailedRef: Not checked: something went wrong on the server (error ID {ref}) and the operation may not have completed. Check the result before deciding whether to retry; if the problem persists, give the error ID to an administrator.
runnerUpgrade.runnerMissing: There is no runner named {name}; nothing was done.
upgradeReason.aiNode: AI runners are not upgraded one by one here: upgrade the kiln-orca connector with npm on the machine
upgradeReason.unsupported: This runner's version does not support per-runner upgrades: install a new version on the machine by hand and run {program} service install once
upgradeReason.noLauncher: It does not run under the launcher (foreground run or an old service entry), so it cannot switch automatically: run {program} service install once on the machine
upgradeReason.disabled: Self-upgrade is turned off locally: upgrade = false in this machine's config.toml
upgradeReason.checkFailed: The latest version is not known yet: {detail}
upgradeReason.notChecked: The latest version is not known yet (the runner queries npm after it connects to the server)
upgradeReason.newer: The current version {current} is newer than the latest release {latest} on npm; not downgrading
upgradeReason.latestChanged: The latest version is now {latest}, not the confirmed {expected}; refresh and confirm again
upgradeReason.noPending: There is no upgrade request in progress
upgradeReason.switching: It has already switched to {version} and is confirming, so it cannot be cancelled; it rolls back automatically if confirmation fails
upgradeReason.unknown: Cannot upgrade (reason {code}): the frontend and kiln-server versions may differ; refresh the page and try again.
runnerCache.formInvalid: The form is invalid; nothing was done.
runnerCache.purgeRequested: Purge request #{id} created: {name} runs it when it has no running jobs, and the result appears below.
runnerCache.purgeFailedRef: Couldn't request the purge: something went wrong on the server (error ID {ref}) and the operation may not have completed. Check the result before deciding whether to retry; if the problem persists, give the error ID to an administrator.
runnerCache.errRepoNotFound: Repository {repo} is not in Kiln, so there is nothing to preview.
cacheNote.noReport: This runner has not reported a cache inventory yet (an old kiln-runner or just registered), so the preview is empty; a purge request still runs on the runner for this scope
cacheNote.report: The preview uses the inventory reported at {at, time}; the purge acts on what is actually on the runner

cacheNote.busy.one: {name} is running {count, number} job: the purge runs after it finishes, and no new jobs are taken meanwhile
cacheNote.busy.other: {name} is running {count, number} jobs: the purge runs after they finish, and no new jobs are taken meanwhile

cacheNote.sharedKept: Shared caches that belong to no single repository (runtimes, CAS, images) are kept and expire on their own schedules

runners.title: Runners
runners.description: Machines that run jobs (kiln-runner); they only make outbound connections to the server. AI reviews and AI development run on Orca + kiln-orca; see <link>AI runners</link>.
runners.helpSummary: What the states, fields, and actions mean
runners.helpConn: Online: contacted the server (to pick up jobs or send a heartbeat) within {offline, duration}. Offline: no contact for more than {offline, duration}; the machine may be off, disconnected, or the service is not running. An offline runner takes no jobs, and its running jobs are treated as "runner lost" once their lease expires (about {lease, duration}). Revoked: the identity is void; it can no longer connect and must be registered again.
runners.helpAccept: Accepting jobs: picks up matching jobs when it has capacity. Paused: takes no new jobs (effective once the runner's current poll ends, at most about {poll, duration}); running jobs continue to completion and are not interrupted. The runner stays connected and can pick up jobs as soon as it is resumed. The pause is stored on the server, so it survives runner restarts; registering again resumes it. Running kiln-runner drain on the machine is a local pause and is not shown here.
runners.helpPool: A group of machines, set by the token at registration. Jobs with pool: X run only on runners in pool X; jobs without a pool can run in any pool.
runners.helpPlatform: The runs-on values (os/arch) the runner can execute, detected when it starts.
runners.helpExecutor: host: runs directly on the machine; oci: runs in a container (only when docker works on the machine); buildkit: can build images (enabled in the runner's config.toml).
runners.helpRunning: Jobs currently assigned to this runner; click one to open its job page.
runners.helpVersion: The kiln-runner version; long values show only the first 12 characters, and the copy button copies the full value.
runners.helpUpgrade: Each runner checks npm hourly for its latest release. When an upgrade is available, an administrator clicks "Upgrade" on the runner's page: the runner downloads and verifies it, switches after its running jobs finish, and rolls back if the new version repeatedly fails to start. Runners not running under the launcher (foreground run or an old service) cannot be upgraded here; run service install once on the machine. upgrade = false in config.toml means self-upgrade is turned off locally.
runners.helpHeartbeat: When it last contacted the server.
runners.helpSpec: The machine's logical CPU count and physical memory, reported each time the runner polls for jobs. This is a static spec, not live usage; older kiln-runner versions don't report it and show "Not reported".
runners.helpAlloc: Allocated is the sum of the resources declared by running jobs (defaults when not declared); allocatable is the machine spec minus what config.toml reserves for the host. When an executor has a fixed limit (the host service's cgroup limit, docker's CPU and memory), the smaller of the two applies. Scheduling accounts by declared resources: allocated plus a new job's declaration never exceeds this capacity, so jobs that don't fit wait in the queue rather than being picked up because the machine looks idle.
runners.helpCache: Total size and report time of the runner's local caches (toolcache, runtimes, git mirrors, images, and so on); click to see the inventory and the last cleanup, where administrators can purge by repository or kind.

runners.revokeNote1: Takes effect immediately: all further requests from {name} are rejected; kiln-runner interrupts its running jobs and exits, and the service does not restart it.

runners.revokeNoteBusy.one: Its {count, number} running job ({jobs}) is interrupted; after about {lease, duration} (when the lease expires) it is treated as "runner lost" and requeued automatically as an infrastructure error for another runner. Jobs with side effects that already started are not retried and are marked failed. If you only want it to stop, "Pause" it first and revoke it after its jobs finish.
runners.revokeNoteBusy.other: Its {count, number} running jobs ({jobs}) are interrupted; after about {lease, duration} (when the lease expires) they are treated as "runner lost" and requeued automatically as infrastructure errors for other runners. Jobs with side effects that already started are not retried and are marked failed. If you only want it to stop, "Pause" it first and revoke it after its jobs finish.

runners.revokeNoteIdle: It has no running jobs right now.
runners.revokeNote3: History (attempts, logs) is kept; it shows as "Revoked" in the list and can be deleted later. Revoking cannot be undone.
runners.revokeNote4: To recover: generate a new registration token, run kiln-runner enroll --name {name} again on this machine, and restart the runner service. Registering under the same name replaces the old identity and brings it back online and accepting jobs.

runnerNew.title: Register a new runner
runnerNew.lead: Complete four steps in order: prepare the machine, generate a one-time registration token, run the commands on the machine, and confirm it is online.
runnerNew.missingText: This address only works for the user who generated the token, and it is not kept after the token has been expired for an hour or after the server restarts. The token is never shown again; generate a new one below if needed.
runnerNew.prepInstall: Install kiln-runner: download {archive} for your platform from Kiln's releases and put the kiln-runner inside it on your PATH (for example /usr/local/bin). Matching the server version is recommended (the server is currently ).
runnerNew.prepHealth: Check that this machine can reach the server: the command below prints ok. The runner only makes outbound connections, so no ports need to be opened.
runnerNew.prepUser: Run the following commands as the regular user that will run the runner, not as root. On Linux, first run sudo loginctl enable-linger "$USER" so user services keep running after you log out.
runnerNew.prepDocker: For container jobs, install docker (OrbStack, colima, or Docker Engine) so that docker info works; without docker only the host executor is available.
runnerNew.prepSecrets: Don't copy the server's admin token or GitHub App private key to this machine; use only the one-time registration token.
runnerNew.prepAI: AI runners (AI review, AI development) don't use kiln-runner; they use a resident Orca on the machine plus the kiln-orca connector. They need Node.js 24+, a running Orca (verified on macOS; Linux can register review and development runners, with hands-on verification in progress), and Codex and/or Claude Code installed and signed in. Git credentials are issued by the server per task, so none are configured on the machine. Docker Compose is optional and starts test services for repositories that need pg or redis. Install the connector with npm:
runnerNew.prepAIAgents: The agent that reviews an AI-developed PR must differ from the one that developed it (for example, Claude Code develops and Codex reviews), so a machine with both agents can register one review runner and one development runner: add {home} to every command for the second one. AI runners can share a machine with kiln-runner.
runnerNew.failedFields: Fix the fields as indicated and generate again.
runnerNew.kindAIReview: kiln-orca: runs only AI reviews of PRs (per the repository's .kiln/agent/config.yml) with Codex or Claude Code in Orca, and can run several tasks at once.
runnerNew.kindAIDev: kiln-orca: picks issues labeled kiln:ready, designs and develops them, and delivers PRs (once the repository enables development). Its PRs are reviewed by a review runner with a different agent; the role can't be changed after registration.
runnerNew.poolCaption: Machine group; leave empty for default. Jobs with pool: X run only on runners in pool X; jobs without a pool can run in any pool.
runnerNew.name: Runner name (optional)
runnerNew.nameCaption: Used only for the commands in step 3; when empty, the machine's hostname is used. Names are unique: registering with an existing runner's name replaces that runner's identity (for re-registering the same machine).
runnerNew.tokenHint: The token is valid for 1 hour, can be used once, and is shown only once after it is generated; refreshing or going back neither generates nor shows it again.
runnerNew.onceTitle: The token is shown only this once
runnerNew.onceText: It won't be shown again or regenerated after you leave or refresh this page. Copy the commands in step 3 now.
runnerNew.shownTitle: The token was already shown and won't be shown again
runnerNew.shownText: If you copied it, run it on the machine; if you didn't save it, generate a new one. An unused earlier token expires on its own.
runnerNew.expiredTitle: The token expired without being used
runnerNew.expiredText: An expired token can't register a runner; generate a new one.
runnerNew.usedText: The token has been used and can't be used again; see step 4.
runnerNew.existingFacts: ({kind}, {conn}) Registering with this name replaces its identity:
runnerNew.existingFactsPool: ({kind}, {conn}, pool {pool}) Registering with this name replaces its identity:
runnerNew.existingRevoked: the revoked {name} comes back online and accepting jobs.
runnerNew.existingActive: the original machine can no longer connect. Continue if this is the same machine being re-registered; otherwise pick another name and generate again.
runnerNew.step3: Run the commands on the machine
runnerNew.cmdEnroll: enroll: registers with the token, named after the machine's hostname (without the domain) unless you add --name.
runnerNew.cmdDoctorAI: doctor: checks the registration, the connection to the server, Orca, agents, git, and Docker (optional).
runnerNew.cmdServiceAI: service install: installs and starts the service (a LaunchAgent on macOS, a systemd user service on Linux); logs are in logs/ under the data directory. You can also run kiln-orca run in the foreground first to watch the output.
runnerNew.cmdHomeAI: If the machine already has an AI runner, add {home} to every command, for example {example}.
runnerNew.cmdDoctor: doctor: checks the platforms, executors, and the connection to the server.
runnerNew.cmdService: service install: installs and starts the service: a LaunchAgent on macOS (starts at boot, logs in ~/kiln/logs/runner.log), a systemd user service on Linux (view logs with journalctl --user -u kiln-runner -f). You can also run kiln-runner run in the foreground first to watch the output.
runnerNew.noCmdUsed: The token has been used, so the commands are no longer shown.
runnerNew.noCmdExpired: The token has expired, so the commands are no longer shown.
runnerNew.noCmdShown: The token was already shown, so the commands are no longer shown.
runnerNew.usedByPool: The token was used by <link>{name}</link> (<ago></ago>, pool {pool}).
runnerNew.notConnected: Registered but not connected yet: run {install} on the machine to start the service, or {run} in the foreground to see the output.
runnerNew.usedGone: The token was used, but that runner no longer exists.
runnerNew.expiredUnused: The token expired and no runner registered with it.
runnerNew.waiting: Waiting for registration: the token hasn't been used yet. This updates automatically after you run the commands from step 3 on the machine.
runnerNew.viewAIList: View in the AI runner list
runnerNew.step3Todo: The commands to run appear after you generate a token.
runnerNew.step4Todo: After the runner registers and starts its service, confirm on the next page or in the <link>runner list</link> that it is online and accepting jobs.

runnerCache.noReportText: Older kiln-runner versions don't report a cache inventory; newer ones report it periodically when idle and after each cleanup.

runnerCache.repoCaption: With a repository selected, only its toolcache, git mirrors, and workspaces are purged.

aiRunners.description: Runners for AI reviews and AI development: Orca on the machine picks up tasks through the kiln-orca connector, and one runner can run several tasks at once. A runner shows as offline after {offline, duration} without contacting the server. For CI runners, see <link>Runners</link>.
